correctness.rationale: A diamond is two triangles sharing an edge. In a rook graph, each triangle lies in a unique row or column clique; thus every diamond lies in one line clique, where D-validity forces pairwise distinct colors for all edges of K_n when n>=4. This establishes binom(n,2) lower bound. For n>=4 the bipartite disjointness graph on unordered 2-subsets of Z/nZ is regular of degree binom(n−2,2)>0; Hall gives a bijection ψ with F∩ψ(F)=∅. Row edge colors {a+i,b+i}; column edge colors a+ψ^−1({i,j}) are injective within lines and cross-incident colors cannot coincide since the former contains a+i and the latter does not. Restriction from R_n,n covers all m≤n. For n=2,3, graph has no diamonds; C4, triangular prism explicit proper colorings, and R_3,3 lower bound 18 edges > 4×floor(9/2), plus checked 5-color certificate. Independent checker verified the R_3,3 certificate; original verifier implements larger finite cases; the infinite proof is Hall plus line-clique geometry.

final_claim: For rook graphs K_m□K_n, 2≤m≤n, the rainbow-diamond proper edge-chromatic index equals 2 for (2,2), 3 for (2,3), 5 for (3,3), and binom(n,2) for every n≥4.
